标题: Kolonos Apartment Fire : Woman Final Cry for Help
正文(前5000): ‘Help, help, I’m drowning!’ — those were the desperate cries heard from a woman found dead alongside a man in an apartment fire in Kolonos, Athens, early Saturday morning (18.04.2026). The blaze broke out under unclear circumstances around 4:30 a.m. on the third floor of a residential building on Argous and Platonos Streets. Panic, Screams, and Rapid Spread According to eyewitnesses, loud voices and a violent argument were heard coming from the apartment shortly before the fire erupted — some even reported sounds of furniture being thrown. Residents described scenes of panic: the woman was seen pounding on the door and shouting for help. Minutes later, flames became visible from neighboring apartments. Emergency Response and Tragic Outcome Firefighters responded immediately with four vehicles and a specialized aerial ladder platform. They managed to extract both individuals unconscious from the smoke-filled unit. Shortly thereafter, their deaths were confirmed. Victims and Background The apartment belongs to an elderly woman who has lived in a nursing home for several years; her son had been residing there. Authorities are currently identifying the male victim — believed to be around 50 years old — with assistance from his aunt, who is present at the police station. Neighbors say both victims were substance users. A neighbor recounted: ‘We heard voices around 5 a.m., then a fierce argument between the man and woman — things crashing, like furniture breaking. Then I heard a woman banging on the door, screaming “Help, I’m drowning!” I went out onto my balcony to see what was happening and heard people in the hallway talking to her, so I went back inside. But the banging and screams continued — then I smelled smoke. I got up and left. I live in the adjacent building, on the first floor. By about 5:20 a.m., we realized something serious was happening. By 5:30, flames were already visible. We saw it start in the right-side apartment on the third floor and quickly spread to the one on the left.’ Footage and Further Details News site newsit.gr has published video footage showing the rapid escalation of the fire in the Kolonos apartment. Neighbors clarified that the woman found with the man was not his sister — but his partner, also approximately 50 years old. For safety reasons, other residents of the building were evacuated. The fire caused extensive damage to the structure. The cause remains officially unknown. Investigators are exploring all possibilities — including a potential gas leak — while the reported altercation prior to the blaze adds further complexity to the case.

标题: 3 die in Uttara apartment fire
正文(前5000): News Flash DHAKA, Jan 16, 2026 (BSS)- At least six people were killed in a devastating fire that broke out in a residential building in the city's Uttara area on Friday morning, authorities confirmed. The six dead included two women, one man and a child. The names and identities of the other deceased are not yet known. The fire erupted around 7:50 am in a flat on the second floor of a six- to seven-storey residential building on Road 18, Sector 11 in Uttara. Fire Service and Civil Defence (FSCD) received the alert at 7:54 am and immediately dispatched firefighting units to the scene. According to FSCD media officer Talha Bin Jasim, two fire units from Uttara Fire Station reached the building by 7:58 am, with more units joining shortly afterward. Firefighters brought the blaze under control around 8:25 am and fully extinguished it by around 10:00 am. Initially, three people were found dead at the scene, while 13 injured residents were taken to Kuwait Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital for treatment. Later, three more victims died while undergoing treatment, raising the death toll to six, said Uttara Division Deputy Commissioner of Police Shahriar Ali. Fire service officials said the fire spread rapidly due to a large amount of furniture inside the affected flat. Md Abdul Mannan, deputy assistant director of Fire Service Dhaka Zone-3, said the fire may have originated from an electrical short circuit, although the exact cause will be confirmed following an investigation. The flames spread from the second floor to the third floor, worsening the situation and filling the building with thick smoke. Local residents described scenes of panic and chaos as occupants struggled to escape the smoke-filled stairwells. Authorities have launched an investigation into the incident and urged?residents to strictly adhere to fire safety measures to prevent similar?tragedies in the future.

标题: Arkadelphia apartment building fire displaces dozens of tenants
正文(前5000): Arkadelphia apartment building fire displaces dozens of tenants ARKADELPHIA, Ark. — An early morning fire on Tuesday left an entire apartment building destroyed and displaced nearly 30 residents in Arkadelphia. According to city officials, emergency crews were called to the Valley View Apartments on Country Club Road around 6:24 a.m. after receiving multiple reports of a fire. The first units with the Arkadelphia Fire Department and Arkadelphia Police Department arrived within minutes, at approximately 6:29 a.m., and immediately began evacuating residents. Early-morning Arkadelphia apartment fire leads to 'total loss' of building Firefighters found heavy flames already consuming the west end of the building, which quickly spread east through the structure. The building, which contained 12 apartments—11 occupied and one vacant—was ultimately declared a total loss. All 27 residents were safely evacuated, and officials reported no major injuries. Arkadelphia Fire Chief Andy Neel said three people were treated at a hospital for minor injuries. "We got a call around 6:24 this morning, structure fire," Neel said. "When units arrived, fire was already coming out of the upstairs apartment. We started searching and trying to get people out of the structure." Neel said the fire likely spread rapidly after reaching the attic space. "We think it got into the attic on the west side," he said. "Once it got in that attic, it just took off. I could see the fire from two or three miles away while I was on my way in." Fire crews worked to get the blaze under control by around 8 a.m., with assistance from seven to eight surrounding departments. Neel noted that the lack of firewalls in the attic made it especially difficult to stop the flames from spreading. During the evacuation, some residents were forced to escape under dangerous conditions. According to officials and witnesses, a wooden staircase in the center of the building was destroyed by flames, forcing some residents to exit from balconies. Resident Mark Brazil, who lived in one of the apartments, said he initially thought the smell of smoke was minor. "I started to smell smoke around 6:20 or 6:30," Brazil said. "I thought maybe someone burned something cooking. But then I heard a loud pop. When I went outside, the whole left half of the apartment complex was on fire." Brazil said he was able to get his dog out safely but was unable to find his cat. "I gave my dog to my roommate and went back in to look for my cat, but I couldn't find her," he said. "This is all I've got right now, but I'm just thankful to be safe." He also described chaotic moments as residents escaped the burning building. "One woman had to toss her child down from the balcony because the stairs were already on fire," Brazil said. "Someone caught the child, and she jumped down after." 标题: Unattended candle cited as London apartment fire does $50K damage
正文(前5000): Unattended candle cited as London apartment fire does $50K damage An unattended candle is the suspected cause of a blaze that did an estimated $50,000 in damage at a London apartment on Tuesday night, London Fire Department officials say. Gary Mosburger, the fire department’s platoon chief manager, said fire crews were called to a highrise apartment building on Kipps Lane in the city’s northeast just after 10 p.m. after residents noticed smoke in the hallways. The fire was contained to a sixth-floor unit and the building was quickly ventilated. No one was home at the unit at the time and there were no injuries. The damage estimate from the fire was set at $50,000. Mosburger said the fire should serve as a safety reminder about candle use and how they should not be left burning when no one is around. “Unattended candles are just not a good idea, ever,” Mosburger said on Wednesday morning, adding there are non-flammable candle alternatives available. 标题: Early morning apartment fire in downtown Lincoln , near Governor Mansion
正文(前5000): Early morning apartment fire in downtown Lincoln, near Governor’s Mansion LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - Lincoln Fire and Rescue responded to an apartment building fire near the Nebraska Governor’s Mansion Wednesday morning. Reports of a structure fire near the intersection of S. 13th and F streets, just one block from the Governor’s Mansion, began coming in around 3:39 a.m. Approximately nine emergency response vehicles were spotted on scene. Footage from the 10/11 Skyview camera showed high flames and thick smoke rising above the tree-line as the first reports came in. No occupants found; fire investigator on scene The building involved is a multi-unit apartment complex that had been previously red-tagged. LFR said the building had been condemned since March 2025. Crews arriving on scene found no occupants inside. LFR did speak with the owner at the scene. The fire was fully involved in one of the upper-level units upon arrival. The fire also made its way into the attic space. A fire investigator is now on scene. It is unknown at this time what caused the fire. 10/11 has a reporter on scene, but this is a developing story, stick with us for more updates as they come in. 标题: 8 - year - old dies in Montgomery apartment fire , two others hospitalized
正文(前5000): 8-year-old dies in Montgomery apartment fire, 2 others hospitalized MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - Montgomery authorities are investigating an early morning apartment fire that killed an 8-year-old boy and critically injured two other people. Multiple fire and rescue units responded to the Woodley Terrace Apartments in the 3900 block of Woodley Road just after 8 a.m. Sunday following reports of a possible structure fire. When responders got to the scene, they found a two-story residential building emitting visible smoke and flames. According to Montgomery Fire/Rescue, the incident quickly escalated to a second alarm, prompting them to mobilize more resources. While searching the building, responders say they found a man and two juveniles inside. All three were taken to a nearby hospital where the 8-year-old died from his injuries. The man and the other juvenile are still in critical condition, according to MFR. Woodley Terrace resident Jabrandon Solomon says he was headed to the store when he noticed the fire. “I seen the smoke, but I thought it was the rent office at first, so I was like, well, I guess it was the rent office up on fire, so I made it halfway down, and it wasn’t the rent office, it was the whole building,” Solomon said. Solomon ran back into the building to try to save as many people as he could. “I ran all the way from the back to the front to go and save the folks, and I was knocking on the doors and dragging folks out and stuff, and I tried to go get the children, but my jacket had caught up on fire, and that’s the end result of that,” he said. “I tried to save everybody.” Residents say the fire alarms failed to go off, and if it weren’t for Solomon, they believe there would have been more fatalities. Councilman Oronde Mitchell told WSFA he has been fighting against apartment complexes he says fail to maintain their buildings to code. “We have to look at the conditions of these apartment complexes,” Mitchell said. “Most of them are owned by out-of-town people and they’re not here to be with the residents. They’re not here to make sure that they find somewhere to stay before the holidays. It’s right before Christmas.” This isn’t a new initiative for Mitchell. “This is what we have been dealing with for the past five years,” he said. “People say why do I go so hard about the conditions of these apartment complexes, and you see the end result. That’s why I try to make sure that the lighting, the metal detectors, the fire detectors are working, because that saves lives.” Monday, Montgomery Public School Superintendent Dr. Zickeyous Byrd released a statement calling for community support: The Montgomery Fire and Rescue Bureau of Investigations is now looking into the cause of the fire. 标题: Fire crews put out 1 - alarm apartment fire in North Miami ; no injuries reporte
正文(前5000): NORTH MIAMI, FLA. (WSVN) - Fire crews put out a fire that burned through an apartment building in North Miami after one hour of work. All 18 units of the apartment complex were rendered uninhabitable due to the fire. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded to the 11600 block of Northeast 18th Drive on Friday evening. 7News cameras captured firefighters battling the flames that were billowing from the roof. Crews had to tear open parts of the roof to vent the fire. “It was a big blaze, as soon as I open my side door, I see that the front door just fell off the hinges due to the blazes.” said Leslie Lagrandeur, an eight-year resident of the complex. Lagrandeur captured the blaze through cell phone video, with the fire erupting in the apartment across from his. Lagrandeur called 911 and reported the fire, and made sure to assist people in the process. “Went door to door knocking on everybody’s door to make sure everybody comes outside.” he said. Extra fire crews were called in to help put out the fire. The blaze forced several residents to evacuate the building. Residents stood across their homes as they watched firefighters try to contain the flames. Some residents were very emotional as they watched their homes erupt in flames. Area resident Julie Avalos said she ran out of her apartment as fast as she could when the fire started. “From corner of the building caught fire and then within under two minutes, the whole building was under smoke. We don’t know where it started but it spread really quickly,” she said. “My uncle managed to go back for our cat, and a neighbor went back for their dog, because they were still inside, and luckily we have our cat, and our neighbor has their dog.” In the aftermath, the owner of the complex, Guy Lorenzo, shared his reaction to the fire, as he dealt with what remains of his property. “The fire came from that apartment there. The door got busted quick, and then the whole inside is burned.” said Lorenzo. “You keep coming back, you know, and then they had to keep going up there, and they keep more water, more water, more water until they can put down the fire.” However, the damage from the fire will remain, and residents are grateful to be alive. “There’s nobody injured, nobody, no deaths, no nothing like that, so, that’s all that matters at that point.” said Lagrandeur. “Everybody gets to enjoy the holidays.” Officials say no injuries were reported from the fire, and investigators are searching into how the fire began. 标题: Westbrook fire displaces residents of North Street apartment building
正文(前5000): At least six residents of a three-unit apartment building in Westbrook were displaced by an intense fire that several crews fought Thursday evening. Westbrook fire Chief Stephen Sloan said the blaze was reported at 71 North St. around 5:20 p.m. Two people were treated for injuries at the site, but no one was seriously hurt or taken to the hospital, he said. Sloan said the fire appears to be accidental but that the Office of State Fire Marshal will investigate the cause. The building will be uninhabitable until it is rebuilt, Sloan said. He did not have an exact count of residents Friday but said it was “upwards of six.” Firefighters had to leave the building shortly after they arrived because of the volume of smoke and fire on all three floors. Instead, they took “a defensive position” and extinguished the fire from outside, Sloan said in a statement Thursday night. Crews from Portland, Scarborough, Windham, Gorham, South Portland and Falmouth helped the Westbrook department extinguish the second-alarm fire. The fire briefly rekindled on the third floor about 1:20 a.m. Friday, but crews quickly extinguished it, Sloan said. By late Friday morning, charred debris — including a mattress and a few small pieces of furniture — could be seen strewn outside the apartment building’s front and side. A large hole was burned in the roof of the green house, and much of the siding along one end was blackened. Sections of North and Brown streets were temporarily closed Thursday evening as firefighters worked at the scene, which was initially cleared about 9 p.m. Five Red Cross volunteers were on the scene and connected with residents of two of the three apartment units. Volunteers are assisting three adults, communications director Jennifer Costa said, but still had one unit to connect with as of Friday morning. The Red Cross is providing disaster-related financial assistance and health services, Costa said. Some of the health services the agency offers include replacing medication or medical equipment, like eyeglasses, that might have gotten lost in the fire, as well as mental health care. Costa said the Red Cross does not know where the displaced residents are staying. The organization also provided snacks and refreshments for 50 to 60 firefighters at the scene.

标题: Claremont apartment fire displaces 10 residents
正文(前5000): CLAREMONT — A Friday night apartment fire displaced about 10 residents due to extensive property damage, a Claremont Fire Department news release said. Firefighters were dispatched to 147 Main St. at 9:30 p.m. on Friday. The four-story residential building had heavy fire showing from the second floor when emergency responders arrived, the release said. After initial suppression efforts, crews found that flames had extended into the attic of the building. The fire was extinguished about 25 minutes after the initial report. Golden Cross Ambulance treated one occupant for minor injuries. Firefighters rescued multiple animals, including dogs, cats and a bearded dragon, Red Cross volunteer George Sykes said by phone Monday. “As far as I know, all the pets were rescued,” said Sykes. While the fire was contained quickly by the emergency crews, the extent of the damage has not yet been formally evaluated, building owner Kevin Lacasse said Monday by phone. The unit where the fire originated suffered the most damage, he said, and the one under it was damaged by water. Multiple other units sustained smoke damage, though most belongings in those homes remained intact, Lacasse added. The building was appraised last year for a sum of $404,000, according to Claremont property records. Lacasse said that the building is insured. Sykes assisted impacted residents, who gathered at the Claremont Fire Department. “Due to significant fire and water damage, the building was deemed unsafe for occupancy,” the news release said. The New Hampshire State Fire Marshal’s Office has been tasked with investigating the cause of the fire, the release said. Windsor and Newport fire crews, Golden Cross Ambulance, and Claremont Police, the Department of Public Works and the city’s building inspector assisted at the scene. Unity and Weathersfield fire departments provided station coverage.

标题: Siblings , ages 1 and 3 , killed in apartment fire
正文(前5000): Siblings, ages 1 and 3, killed in apartment fire BOWLING GREEN, Ky. (WBKO/Gray News) - Two young children died after a fire tore through a unit at a Kentucky apartment building. The fire started in the early morning on March 12 at a Bowling Green apartment, the fire department said. The two children who died were identified by family members as 3-year-old Dominic and his 1-year-old sister, Aura. The victims’ aunt, Destaney Handy, said the children’s mother woke to the smell of smoke and discovered the apartment was on fire. “My sister, when I was talking to her yesterday, she just said she woke up from the smell of smoke and realized that her apartment was on fire. She just kept saying to me, ‘Destaney, I tried to get to them. I tried to get to them,’” Handy said. Handy, who lives in Iowa, said she had not yet met Dominic or Aura in person, but had plans to visit them this summer. “Since I live so far away from them, I hadn’t had the opportunity yet to be able to go out there to meet them. I just don’t know how to fathom that the only time I’m going to be able to see them is in a casket. I never got to hold them. I never got to meet them, but from everything that I know and from everything that I’ve learned, they were amazing. They were amazing kids,” Handy said. Handy described the family’s state as devastated. “She’s just devastated. We’re all just devastated. This is like something that feels unreal, like it’s some kind of nightmare that we’re hoping that we can wake up from,” Handy added. Handy created a GoFundMe to help cover funeral costs for Dominic and Aura. The family said they appreciate the community’s continued support. Copyright 2026 WBKO via Gray Local Media, Inc. 标题: Gwinnett County apartment fire displaces more than 3 dozen people
正文(前5000): Gwinnett County apartment fire displaces more than 3 dozen people GWINNETT COUNTY, Ga. - Two dozen people have been displaced following a Sunday night fire at a Gwinnett County apartment complex, according to officials. What we know: The Gwinnett County Fire Department said firefighters responded to the Las Palmas Apartments at 2113 Seasons Parkway around 10:03 p.m. after multiple 911 calls about a fire. When they arrived, firefighters said the three-story apartment building had heavy fire and smoke coming from it. Firefighters used ground hoses and aerial apparatus to fight the flames. By 10:31 p.m., officials said the fire was under control. According to fire officials, the fire affected six apartment units. Four were a total loss, and two had heavy damage. The fire did not spread to the adjacent building. Nobody was injured in the fire, but 40 people have been displaced. Officials said a person who lived in one of the apartments told firefighters they heard a "pop" noise, went to check it out, and discovered the fire. That person then alerted everyone in the building. Dig deeper: Officials said there were no working smoke alarms in the apartments affected by the fire. What we don't know: Fire investigators said the fire began in the back of a second-story unit. Fire investigators could not access the area of origin because of a structural collapse. The fire’s cause is officially listed as undetermined. What's next: Gwinnett County Office of Emergency Management and Hopewell Missionary Baptist Church joined fire officials to assist displaced residents.
